findings.title: website_name bypasses TL0 website hiding
findings.body: include_website_name is missing the trailing ? that ActiveModel::Serializers uses (every other include hook in this file is include_*?), so the method is never called and website_name is always serialized. website_name is also absent from untrusted_attributes, which is what hides website, bio, and location for trust-level 0 users viewed anonymously. The profile template now renders model.website_name, so an anonymous visitor still sees a new user's site host and path even though website itself is omitted. That undoes the anti-spam/privacy gate. Add website_name to untrusted_attributes (which defines include_website_name?) and drop the dead include_website_name method; the serializer spec never covers a TL0 user who has a website.

findings.title: Same-site host check is case-sensitive and www-asymmetric
findings.body: website_host is compared to Discourse.current_hostname with == and ends_with? without downcasing. Ruby's URI does not lowercase the host, so http://Example.com/user on an example.com forum fails every branch and website_name is only Example.com, not Example.com/user. The same gap hits the common www vs apex pair: www.example.com (3 labels) vs example.com (2 labels) skips the equal-length sibling branch, and example.com.ends_with?('.www.example.com') is false, so the path is dropped. The reverse (forum on www, website on the apex) does show the path via ends_with?, so the feature is inconsistent for the same site. Normalize both hosts (downcase, and treat a single leading www label as equivalent) before comparing, and cover those cases in the serializer spec.
